interview_questions.question: What is Product management, and why does it matter in product, project or program management?
interview_questions.preferred_answer: Product management is the discipline of understanding customer problems, defining product direction, prioritizing investments, and coordinating cross-functional work to create sustainable customer and business value.

practical_scenarios.title: Founder demands a competitor feature
practical_scenarios.situation: A founder wants an expensive AI feature immediately because a competitor announced one.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Reframe the request as a customer and strategic hypothesis, identify the decision deadline, gather rapid evidence, compare opportunity cost, propose a reversible test and communicate what would justify scaling.

practical_scenarios.title: Conflicting enterprise customers
practical_scenarios.situation: Two major customers demand mutually incompatible workflow changes.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Clarify underlying needs, revenue and retention exposure, segment fit and architecture impact; explore configurable or segment-specific options; make a transparent product strategy decision rather than promising both.

practical_scenarios.title: Discovery invalidates the approved solution
practical_scenarios.situation: Research shows users do not have the problem that funded the project.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Escalate the evidence, protect sunk-cost neutrality, revisit the business case, propose alternative problems or stop criteria, and record the governance decision.

practical_scenarios.title: Ambiguous experiment result
practical_scenarios.situation: An A/B test improves clicks but reduces successful task completion.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Use the pre-defined primary and guardrail measures, assess segment and statistical uncertainty, avoid cherry-picking, investigate mechanism and decide whether to stop, redesign or run a follow-up test.

practical_scenarios.title: Sales promised a roadmap date
practical_scenarios.situation: Sales committed a feature to a customer before engineering validation.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Assess strategic value, contract and relationship impact, create a forecast range and scope options, identify dependencies, decide at the correct authority level and reset external communication with one owner.

practical_scenarios.title: Critical-path milestone slips
practical_scenarios.situation: A critical-path activity slips three weeks and the sponsor says the final date cannot move.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Recalculate the network and forecast, identify true constraints, evaluate fast-tracking, crashing and scope options with cost and risk, and obtain an explicit trade-off decision.
evaluation_criteria: Escalates decision rather than accepting impossible demand

practical_scenarios.title: Single-source vendor delay
practical_scenarios.situation: A critical vendor misses two milestones and provides optimistic updates without evidence.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Enforce contractual reporting and acceptance, independently validate progress, activate contingency and alternate sourcing analysis, update risk exposure and involve procurement, legal and sponsor governance.
evaluation_criteria: Maintains relationship without accepting unsupported claims

practical_scenarios.title: Executive scope creep
practical_scenarios.situation: An executive repeatedly adds “small” requests while rejecting schedule changes.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Log and group changes, show cumulative scope, cost, schedule and risk impact, use agreed thresholds and change authority, and ask the executive to choose among scope, time, cost or benefit trade-offs.
evaluation_criteria: Avoids silent overtime as a solution

practical_scenarios.title: Cost overrun with good progress
practical_scenarios.situation: The project is delivering planned scope but CPI is 0.78.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Validate earned value and actual cost data, identify causes, forecast EAC, separate one-time from systemic variance, analyze alternatives and update the funding or scope decision before reserves are exhausted.
evaluation_criteria: Links corrective action to root cause

practical_scenarios.title: Quality versus launch date
practical_scenarios.situation: Severe but low-frequency defects remain before a public launch.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Assess customer harm, detectability, legal and reputational risk, define non-negotiable quality thresholds, consider phased rollout or feature disablement, and ensure the accountable authority accepts residual risk.

practical_scenarios.title: Security issue discovered pre-release
practical_scenarios.situation: A penetration test identifies a high-severity vulnerability two days before launch.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Pause affected release scope, engage security and incident governance, validate exposure, remediate and retest or use a safe workaround, communicate impact and preserve evidence.

practical_scenarios.title: Sprint repeatedly fails its goal
practical_scenarios.situation: A Scrum Team completes many tasks but misses its Sprint Goal for three Sprints.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Inspect goal clarity, work selection, dependencies, interruptions, Definition of Done and team capacity; reduce WIP, create stronger Sprint Goals and address systemic impediments in the retrospective and organization.

practical_scenarios.situation: Three teams use different cadences and one shared API is late.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Create an integrated dependency and interface plan, assign owners and dates, validate contract and test environments, sequence decoupling options and establish cross-team escalation and review.

practical_scenarios.situation: A program delivered its systems but service cost and customer satisfaction did not improve.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Revisit the benefits map and assumptions, verify adoption and process change, identify disbenefits and operational barriers, hold benefit owners accountable and redirect or close components based on evidence.

practical_scenarios.situation: Forecast benefits have fallen below remaining cost, but senior leaders are emotionally invested.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Present updated business case and opportunity cost, separate sunk costs, offer stop, pause, pivot and continue options, document risks and request a formal governance decision.

practical_scenarios.situation: Teams see the PMO as a reporting police function and submit low-quality data.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Interview PMO customers, remove non-decision reporting, standardize essential data, automate collection, offer useful forecasting and risk support, and measure whether decisions and delivery improve.

practical_scenarios.situation: An AI summary incorrectly says a regulatory dependency is resolved.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Stop distribution, verify source records, correct the report, assess who acted on it, document the incident, strengthen access and prompt controls, and require human approval for material status.

practical_scenarios.title: Pressure to hide red status
practical_scenarios.situation: A sponsor asks the manager to mark a project amber because red status may affect funding.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Explain the reporting criteria and consequence of misrepresentation, present the factual status with recovery options, document the request and escalate through ethics or governance channels if pressure continues.

evaluation_rubric.evidence: Frames problems, validates needs, connects choices to customer and business outcomes.
Integrates scope, schedule, cost, risk, quality, resources and change with realistic forecasting.
Manages benefits, interdependencies, strategic alignment, capacity and investment trade-offs.
Uses empiricism, feedback, flow, Scrum/Kanban concepts and appropriate tailoring without process theater.
Communicates decisions, negotiates conflict, builds teams and influences without relying only on authority.
Uses trustworthy measures, experiments, economics, EVM and decision-relevant analysis.
Reports honestly, manages conflicts, applies proportionate controls and keeps accountable humans in the loop.
